text: dsh-peak-cost 是一个适用于 DeepSeek Harness 网页端的插件：它把会话费用信息放到输入框下方的 composer dock，并由宿主会话投影汇总已完成模型调用的费用。界面显示当前是否处于高峰时段、会话累计美元估算、账户余额，以及按网页结果、工具结果、消息和模型输出等类别拆分的花费。悬停可查看首次计费与缓存重发费用。适合希望在运行会话时了解费用构成的用户；余额通过宿主账户接口可选读取，不需插件单独配置 API key。

dsh-peak-cost adds a dock below the DeepSeek Harness composer. It shows peak status and session spend from model usage. Hover for first-time and cached costs by content category. The host account interface can supply the balance. No plugin-specific API key is declared.
想在聊天输入框旁边随时看到当前会话大概花了多少钱。
能不能把模型费用按工具结果、网页内容和回复分别算出来？
Show me whether DeepSeek is in peak billing hours and how much this session has spent.
dsh-peak-cost 的功能「会话费用与时段状态」：在 composer dock 展示高峰或非高峰状态和本会话累计费用；宿主投影依据模型、调用时间和上报用量计算费用。进入会话后自动显示。
dsh-peak-cost 的功能「类别费用明细与余额」：悬停 dock 状态可展开费用面板，按内容类别区分首次计费和缓存重发，并在宿主账户接口可用时显示余额。
使用前须知：余额是通过 DSH 宿主的 remote.account.getBalance 接口读取，接口不可用时余额不显示；源码未声明插件专用 API key 或环境变量。

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/en/guide/quickstart) plugin that adds one ambient line under the composer:

```text
● Off-peak · ≈ $0.338 · bal $7.27
```

It answers three questions about the session you are in:

dsh-peak-cost README · dsh-peak-cost：1. **Is DeepSeek billing in peak hours right now?**
2. **How much has this session cost so far, in US dollars?**
3. **What is left in your DeepSeek account?**

Hovering the line opens a panel with the cost attribution: the billing window and the time until it flips, the account balance and both wallets, and a per-category table showing what each kind of content cost when it first entered the context versus what it costs on every later call that re-sends it.

dsh-peak-cost README · dsh-peak-cost：The screenshot above is unedited: the line sits beside the shipped turn/step counter and token meter, and reads `● Off-peak · ≈ $0.338 · bal $7.27` for a session at 9 turns and 264 steps with a 99.6% cache hit rate.

dsh-peak-cost README · Behavior：| | |
|---|---|
| Slot | `conversation.composer.dock` (below the composer card, beside the shipped activity and context-usage entries) |
| Scope | Per session |
| Updates | Spend follows every settled model call; the status label re-evaluates against the clock every 30 s; the balance refreshes every 60 s |
| Locales | English and Chinese, following the app's language setting |

dsh-peak-cost README · Balance：Next to the session estimate the line also shows your DeepSeek account balance:

```text
● Off-peak · ≈ $0.18 · bal ¥7.26
```

It is read from the Host's account Remote (`ctx.remote.account.getBalance`) every 60 seconds and whenever the window regains focus — the same call the Settings → Account page makes — and **both wallet kinds are summed**: the recharge wallet plus any bonus/grant wallet, which is why it can differ from a single number on a top-up page. The panel always lists both.

dsh-peak-cost README · Balance：The account face is a Typert Remote namespace rather than a plain service, so the plugin captures it through a scoped `ctx.inject(['remote.account'], …)` and still falls back to `ctx.remote.account` on the root context. That keeps it independent of load order: the cost line renders immediately, and the balance appears as soon as the transport is reachable.

dsh-peak-cost README · Balance：The balance is optional in every direction: a signed-out account, an API-key-only setup, a failed read, or a build without the account transport all simply drop it, leaving the cost line intact. Nothing is cached to disk.

dsh-peak-cost README · Where the money went：Hovering the line opens a themed panel (fixed-positioned above the composer, closes on leave or Escape) with the attribution:

```text
Content            In context   First time   Re-sent
Tool results            40k         $0.021   $0.0047
Web results             18k         $0.0014  $0.0110
Assistant replies       12k         $0.0048  $0.00

Each row answers two different questions:

dsh-peak-cost README · Where the money went：- **First time** — what that content cost when it entered the context, billed as cache-miss input, once.
- **Re-sent** — what it has cost on every later call that carried it, billed as cache-hit input.

dsh-peak-cost README · Where the money went：So "what did the web search data cost in this session?" is one row: the first fetch at the miss rate plus every re-send at the hit rate. A search result that arrives once and stays in the conversation is billed as input exactly once and as cache for the rest of the session — which is why 18k tokens of web data cost about a cent rather than 18 × the input rate.

dsh-peak-cost README · How the split is made：Per-call totals are the provider's own numbers, so category costs add up to the real bill and only the split between categories is an estimate (four characters per token). Output is listed separately because it is not context. Replaced or compacted content is subtracted as it leaves the context, so the "In context" column tracks the live surface rather than a running sum.

dsh-peak-cost README · Install：The package is a Harness **bundle**: it declares `dsh.bundle.patch` and a `dsh.client` half, so installing it in a profile mounts both the Host projection and the Web entry.

Install the package spec `github:ogidimitrov/dsh-peak-cost` as a bundle — from the Plugins page of the app, or from an agent session through the plugin manager's `install_bundle` action with that spec as the target.

dsh-peak-cost README · Install：The plugin needs a Harness build that provides the session projection registry, the `conversation.composer.dock` slot, and the client locale service — that is, the current DeepSeek Harness desktop/web app. It has no npm dependencies and no build step.

To remove it, uninstall the bundle from the same Plugins page.

dsh-peak-cost README · How the number is computed：Money is not inferred on the client from a token total. The Host half folds the durable session log and registers one session projection, `peakCost`, whose wire view carries the cumulative spend. The Client renders that value; it never re-folds events, so the figure survives paging, reloads, and compaction.

Each `assistant/message` in the log is priced on its own:
dsh-peak-cost README · How the number is computed：Because the fold is a pure function of committed events, replay and fork produce the same figure.

dsh-peak-cost README · Cache hits are part of the calculation：Harness sends the whole conversation on every model call, so a long session burns a large prompt each time — and nearly all of it is a **cache hit**, billed at the hit rate rather than the input rate. That discount is the whole reason one session can move millions of prompt tokens for cents.

A real session from this plugin, mid-conversation, off-peak on `deepseek-flash`:
section: Cache hits are part of the calculation

text:
dsh-peak-cost README · Cache hits are part of the calculation：| | tokens | rate (off-peak) | cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| cache-miss input | 184,312 | $0.15 / 1M | $0.028 |
| cache-hit input | 21,805,952 | $0.003 / 1M | $0.065 |
| output | 102,878 | $0.60 / 1M | $0.062 |
| **total** | | | **$0.155** |

The same 22M prompt tokens billed without prompt caching would be **$3.36** at the miss rate; the per-row **First time** / **Re-sent** split in the panel shows the same discount for the session you are looking at.
section: Cache hits are part of the calculation

text: dsh-peak-cost README · Why this number and your balance can disagree：The figure is a **list-price equivalent**, computed from the session log; it never reads your wallet. Three things make a wallet diverge from it:
section: Why this number and your balance can disagree

text:
dsh-peak-cost README · Why this number and your balance can disagree：- **Granted or bonus credit is consumed first.** DeepSeek deducts from granted/bonus balances before a topped-up balance, so a topped-up number can stay flat while usage accrues.
- **The balance is not streamed.** It is read on demand from the platform; a panel left open shows what it read.
- **Not every call is in the log.** Session-title generation and some compaction work never commit an `assistant/message`, so they cost money this estimate cannot see.
section: Why this number and your balance can disagree

text: dsh-peak-cost README · Why this number and your balance can disagree：Use the platform's usage page for the authoritative charge; this line is for watching a session's shape while it runs.
section: Why this number and your balance can disagree

text:
dsh-peak-cost README · Rates and calendar：Defaults follow [DeepSeek's published pricing](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing/) (USD per 1M tokens):

| Model | Cache hit | Cache miss | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| `deepseek-flash` | 0.006 | 0.30 | 1.20 |
| `deepseek-v4-pro` | 0.044 | 1.32 | 3.96 |

Peak hours are **01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 UTC, Monday through Friday**, excluding Chinese public holidays. Every other hour, all weekend, and Chinese public holidays are off-peak. Off-peak prices are half of the table above.
dsh-peak-cost README · Rates and calendar：Legacy aliases (`deepseek-v4-flash`, and the older `-chat` / `-reasoner` names) bill at the flash card.

dsh-peak-cost README · Known limitations：- **An estimate.** It prices reported tokens at list rates. It is not a bill: nothing here reads your balance or the provider's invoice.
- **Only settled model calls count.** Calls that never commit an `assistant/message` — session-title generation, some compaction work — are not in the log and are not counted. Failed attempts that report usage without a settled message are likewise skipped.
- **One session.** Subagent sessions have their own logs and their own dock lines; this number is the session you are looking at.
- **Unknown routes.** A model id that matches no card is counted in the message total but priced at zero; the tooltip reports how many.
- **Search/Fetch.** Standalone Search and Fetch API charges are not modelled.

dsh-peak-cost README · Development：```bash
npm test        # node --test: fold semantics, window edges, wire schema, client rendering
```
